title: Lion's Guide Question Bank Plan and First Draft
status: Draft for team review - not approved for publication

source.page_numbering: Page numbers refer to the 92-page downloaded PDF collection, not the individual online handbook sections.
source.authority_note: The collection states that the online handbook remains the binding version. This draft uses the downloaded collection; current online policies have not been rechecked.

proposal.summary: Lion's Guide will help students find reviewed handbook answers through a curated question bank. Students can type in their own words, but the website will suggest standard questions instead of answering free-form input directly. No AI service is required for this approach.
student_flow: A student types a question or a few words into the search box.
The website shows up to five question-bank suggestions under 'Are you asking about...'. Alternative wording and common spelling mistakes help find suggestions.
The student must select one standard question before an answer appears. Pressing Enter without a selection shows suggestions, not an answer or a guessed PDF page.
The answer shows a short explanation, applicable conditions and exceptions, original handbook excerpts, and links to the cited PDF pages.
Every suggestion list includes 'None of these match my question'. Students can browse categories or submit a question anonymously.
Submitted questions enter a team review queue. They do not become public questions or answers automatically.
editorial_rules: Publish only answers that the team has checked against the handbook and reviewed for conditions and exceptions.
Keep the selected question visible beside its answer so students can check that it matches their situation.
Question suggestions are possible matches, not a claim that the website understands every free-form sentence.
Do not treat an unmentioned situation as permission. Explain when the handbook does not provide a clear answer.
Keep alternative wording specific to each question. Do not treat all questions containing 'phone', 'late', or 'AI' as the same intent.
Provide category browsing and 'None of these match my question' when matching is weak or irrelevant.

Do not require names or email addresses on the new-question form. Do not promise individual replies. Check the chosen form service's metadata and retention behavior before describing submissions as fully anonymous.
Review the question bank when the school changes a cited policy. Keep a source reference and review date for each published answer.
All student-facing interface text, standard questions, and answers will be in English.
review_checks: A hoodie question should suggest the approved sweatshirt question, not an unrelated dress-code paragraph.
A vague phone question should offer separate school-use and storage questions without showing an answer first.
A phone-repair question, a missed-flight question, and an AI-pizza question must not automatically open school-policy answers.
A question with no suitable match must still offer category browsing and anonymous submission.
Exact-boundary and contradictory-source questions must remain on hold until the school clarifies them.

editorial_questions.issue: An isolated 'ONLY OCS' line appears between the hats and shoes paragraphs. Confirm whether this limits outdoor hats to OCS-branded hats.
Page 63 says a tardy is up to 15 minutes and an absence is more than 15 minutes; page 65 says 15 minutes or more is an unexcused absence. Confirm how exactly 15 minutes is recorded.

The general paragraph says previously assigned tests should be taken on the return day, while the assessment subsection allows five school days or an agreed teacher arrangement. Confirm scope before adding a standalone makeup-deadline FAQ.
The excessive-tardy sequence contains 'Twenty (25) class tardies'. Confirm the intended count before drafting a full escalation schedule.

The OCS AI Stance at a Glance table is embedded as an image and missing from handbook.json. Its cited passages below were visually transcribed from the PDF. The separate linked AI Philosophy and Guidelines DOCX has not been reviewed, so no more detailed AI permissions are inferred.

Online translators in foreign-language classes are listed under cheating, while the general software/AI paragraph mentions teacher approval. Confirm the scope of any teacher-authorized translation exception.

conditions: A college sweatshirt must be a solid color and clearly display the college or university name.
The college-sweatshirt option is stated for juniors and seniors.
A sweatshirt does not replace the required polo or Oxford underneath.
Special non-uniform dress requires Office of Student Life permission; follow event-specific instructions.

sources.quote: Students may wear an approved OCS athletic/spirit/leadership sweatshirt over an Oaks polo or oxford.
Juniors and Seniors may also wear a collegiate sweatshirt, over an Oaks polo or oxford, which must be a solid color and distinctly display the name of the college/university.
Permission for special non-uniform dress is only granted by the Office of Student Life.

questions.question: Can I wear joggers, sweatpants, or athletic shorts on a normal school day?
alternative_wording: Can I wear sweats?

Outside that active participation, students are expected to be in school uniform during school hours.
Special non-uniform dress needs permission from the Office of Student Life.

sources.quote: NO athletic shorts, sweatpants or joggers (this includes OC joggers/sweatpants/shorts)
Students are expected to be in school uniform during school hours unless the student is actively participating in a dance class or strength & conditioning class.

slippers, slides or shoes with a heel more than two inches are never allowed to be worn by students at school.

alternative_wording: What is the first dress-code consequence?
Do I have to change clothes?
Will my parents be told about a uniform violation?

conditions: Students who do not follow uniform guidelines are sent to the Office of Student Life.

questions.question: How should my parent or guardian report an absence?
alternative_wording: How do I call in sick?
Where do my parents report that I am absent?
Can my parent report my absence in AXIS?
How long do we have to clear an absence?
questions.short_answer: A parent or guardian should report the absence in AXIS, the preferred method. The handbook also lists the Attendance Office email for reporting after an absence has occurred. Absences must be cleared within 72 hours.
conditions: Parents should inform the school ahead of time when possible.
The listed email is agreason@oakschristian.org; check that this contact is still current before publication.
A student cannot rely on reporting the absence personally instead of parent or guardian communication.
An unreported absence can affect credit for assignments and assessments.

sources.quote: PREFERRED: Record absence/early release/or late arrival in AXIS.
Only to be used after absence has occurred: Email (agreason@oakschristian.org)
Parents must clear a student’s absence within 72 hours using AXIS or contacting the school attendance officer.
When it becomes necessary for a student to miss school, parents are expected to inform the school, if possible, ahead of time.

questions.question: When is arriving late counted as an absence instead of a tardy?
alternative_wording: What if I am 15 minutes late?
How late counts as absent?
What is the difference between tardy and absent?
I arrived after class started - how is it recorded?
questions.short_answer: The handbook links the attendance classification to how many minutes late you arrive. Its wording at exactly 15 minutes is inconsistent, so the Attendance Office needs to confirm that boundary before this answer is published.
conditions: Page 63 defines a class tardy as up to 15 minutes late and an absence as more than 15 minutes late.
Page 65 instead says 15 minutes or more is an unexcused absence.
Page 63 says the Attendance Office can determine whether an absence is parent reported. Do not promise that being parent reported removes all attendance or academic consequences.

sources.quote: Class tardy is defined as being up to fifteen (15) minutes late to a specific class. A student is considered absent if they are more than fifteen (15) minutes late to a class.
If a student is late to class by 15 minutes or more, this will be considered an unexcused absence.

questions.question: Is being late because of traffic or car trouble an excused tardy?
alternative_wording: Does traffic excuse being late?
My carpool was late - is that excused?
What if the car broke down?
Is oversleeping an excused tardy?
questions.short_answer: Traffic, transportation or carpool issues, car problems, and sleeping in are listed as unexcused reasons for tardiness.
conditions: A parent reporting an issue does not by itself turn it into a school-approved reason.
The handbook asks families to contact the Office of Student Life when tardies are outside their control; the office handles the individual situation.

sources.quote: Unexcused tardies include: sleeping in transportation/carpool issues car problems traffic schedule mix-up
Students and parents are asked to notify the Office of Student Life if there is a situation where the tardies are outside of their control.

alternative_wording: How do I check out early?
Can my parent call to pick me up?
Can I drive myself to an appointment?
How far ahead do we report an early release?
questions.short_answer: A parent must report the reason and departure time in AXIS at least two hours ahead, or release may be delayed. Do not leave before the Attendance Office verifies parental permission.
conditions: Provide proof of the appointment when returning to school, such as a doctor's note.
A parent picking up a student must be verified at the front desk.
If you drive yourself, a parent must still inform the Attendance Office before release.
The handbook says students will not be released during lunch based on a parent phone call. Off-campus privileges follow separate rules.

sources.quote: Parents must report an early release using AXIS, with the reason and time of departure, at least two hours in advance, or there may be a delay in the student’s departure.
If a student leaves prior to parental permission verified by the attendance office, they will be considered truant.
Students who are driving themselves to an appointment must have a parent inform the attendance office prior to their release.

questions.question: Can missing a test affect my grade even if my parent reports the absence?
alternative_wording: Does a parent note remove a missed-test penalty?
What happens if I am absent on a test day?
Will an excused absence on a quiz day affect my grade?
Is there a penalty for repeatedly missing assessments?
questions.short_answer: Yes. The Parent Reported/Excused Absence subsection says the first assessment-day absence receives a warning, and each subsequent assessment-day absence results in a 15% assessment penalty. Exceptions require administration approval.
conditions: This answer concerns the parent-reported or excused assessment-day rule; unexcused absences have a separate penalty rule.
The same section has makeup deadlines and additional rules for repeatedly missed AP or Honors assessments. Confirm your actual situation with the teacher and school administration.
The source contains two differently worded makeup-deadline rules. This answer does not promise an automatic five-day extension.

sources.section: Missed Assessment Classes/Day - Parent Reported/Excused Absence
sources.quote: Students who are absent on an assessment day, even if it is parent reported, will receive a warning for the first absence. Each subsequent absence on an assessment day will result in a grade penalty of 15% on the assessment.
Any exception to this rule must be made by administration

questions.question: Can I attend practice or a game if I miss Chapel, Community Assembly, or Advisory?
alternative_wording: Can I skip chapel and still practice?
Does missing advisory affect sports?
Can I perform after missing assembly?
Does a parent excuse let me play after missing chapel?
questions.short_answer: The handbook says students who miss Chapel, Community Assembly, or Advisory may not participate in school athletics, arts, or other school activities that day. This includes practices and contests, as well as performances and rehearsals.
conditions: The Chapel and Community Assembly paragraph on page 63 says this applies to absence for any reason; do not assume parent reporting restores eligibility.
Separate daily-attendance and unserved-detention rules can also affect eligibility. Confirm your status with the Office of Student Life.

sources.quote: Students who do not attend Chapel, Community Assembly, or Advisory will NOT be allowed to participate in school athletics (practices and contests), the arts (performances and rehearsals), nor any other school activities that day.

sources.section: Participation in Athletics, Arts, and School Activities
sources.quote: Any student who is absent from Chapel or Community Assembly, for any reason, will NOT be allowed to participate in athletics

questions.question: Can I use my phone during lunch, passing periods, or outside during the school day?
alternative_wording: Can I check my phone at lunch?
Can I text between classes?
Can I use my phone outside?
When must my phone be off?
questions.short_answer: The general rule prohibits student cell-phone use throughout the school day, stated as 8:30 a.m. to 3:15 p.m., both indoors and outdoors. It is not limited to class time.
conditions: The phone must be turned off and stored for the school day.
Page 70 provides a narrow exception for phone use during Chapel or an assembly when the Office of Student Life instructs students to do so. This is not a general lunch or passing-period exception.
Confirm any individual special arrangement directly with the Office of Student Life; none is granted by this FAQ.

sources.quote: the use of cell phones by students during the school day (8:30am-3:15pm), whether inside school buildings or in outdoor areas, is prohibited.

sources.section: Guidelines for the Use of Electronic Devices
sources.quote: Cell phones may not be used during chapel, community assembly, or an indoor assembly unless instructed to do so by the Office of Student Life.

questions.question: Can I keep my phone in my pocket if it is switched off?
alternative_wording: Can I carry my phone on me?
Does turning off my phone make pocket storage okay?
Where should I put my phone?
Can my phone stay in my backpack?
questions.short_answer: No. During the school day, phones must be off and stored in a backpack, locker, or vehicle. The handbook explicitly says phones may not be on a student's person.
conditions: Turning a phone off does not remove the separate storage rule.
The rule applies during the school day, not just while a class is in session.

sources.section: Guidelines for the Use of Electronic Devices
sources.quote: Phones should be off and stored at the beginning of each school day. Devices may be stored in backpacks, lockers, or vehicles. Phones may not be on a student’s person at any time during the school day.

sources.quote: Headphones/earbuds/Air pods may not be worn during the school day.

questions.question: Can I use my laptop to take notes or do assignments in class?
alternative_wording: Can I bring my own laptop?
Can I take notes on a computer?

conditions: Students are responsible for the safety and security of devices they bring.

sources.quote: Personal laptop computers may be used for taking notes and for assignments at the teacher’s discretion.

alternative_wording: Can AI write my homework?
Is ChatGPT allowed for schoolwork?

questions.short_answer: Do not present AI-assisted or software-generated work as your own authentic work without teacher approval. The handbook's AI overview also says AI used in the generative process must be acknowledged through citation.
conditions: Confirm the teacher's instructions for the actual assignment; do not assume permission carries over to other work.
Citation does not replace the teacher-approval requirement.
The overview says Large Language Model use should be primarily reserved for junior- and senior-level classes; it does not give automatic permission based on grade level.
The PDF links a fuller AI Philosophy and Guidelines document. Its detailed permissions have not been incorporated into this draft.

sources.quote: The use of artificial intelligence (chatGPT, Photomath, Google translate, Calculator, etc.) is not allowed to be presented as authentic work without teacher approval.

sources.section: OCS AI Stance at a Glance - Timeline

questions.question: Is copying homework or letting a friend copy my work an academic-integrity violation?
alternative_wording: Can I copy a friend's homework?
Can I give someone my answers?
Is letting someone copy just as serious?
Can I send a completed assignment to a friend?
questions.short_answer: Yes. Copying homework or classwork is listed as cheating. Allowing someone else to copy is listed as facilitating academic dishonesty, and the handbook says the helper is equally responsible for the violation.
conditions: The policy also addresses sharing completed assignments from a previous semester or year.
Ask your teacher what collaboration is permitted; do not treat legitimate group work and copying completed answers as the same activity.

sources.quote: Copying homework or other class work.
Such students are equally as guilty of an academic integrity violation as the recipients of their aid.
Allowing another person to copy homework or other class work.

questions.question: Can I submit the same essay or project for two different classes?
alternative_wording: Can I reuse an old essay?

Can I reuse a big part of another assignment?
questions.short_answer: Not without permission. The handbook lists submitting the same work, or major portions of it, for two classes without permission as cheating.
conditions: The rule covers major portions of the same work, not only an identical complete submission.

The quoted rule specifically concerns two classes. It does not establish a blanket rule for every possible reuse of old work.

sources.quote: Submitting the same work or major portions of the same work for two classes without permission.

questions.question: Do I still need to cite a source if I put its ideas into my own words?
alternative_wording: Does paraphrasing need a citation?
Do I cite an article if I rewrite it?
Can I summarize a website without citing it?

questions.short_answer: Yes. Summarizing or paraphrasing another person's ideas without acknowledging the source is listed as plagiarism. Rewriting the wording does not remove the need to credit the idea's source.
conditions: Directly using another writer's words also requires quotation marks.
Include a bibliography or works-cited page when the assignment requires one.
Ask the teacher which citation format to use if the assignment instructions do not specify it.

sources.quote: Summarizing or paraphrasing another’s idea, thought, or concept without acknowledging the source.
Neglecting to place quotation marks around another writer’s words.
Omitting a source citation for another’s idea or failing to include a bibliography or works cited page when requested for an assignment.
